overview.title: Cosmology: Understanding the Universe
overview.description: The origin, evolution, and ultimate fate of the universe

bigBang.description: The universe began from an infinitely hot, dense point
bigBang.notAnExplosion: Not an explosion in space, but expansion of space itself
evidence: Abundance of light elements (hydrogen, helium, lithium)

timeline.0: Planck epoch - quantum gravity dominates (10^-43 seconds)
timeline.10^-6: Quark epoch ends, protons and neutrons form
timeline.3 minutes: Big Bang Nucleosynthesis - light elements form

cosmicInflation.description: Universe expanded exponentially in fraction of a second
cosmicInflation.expansion: Grew from subatomic to grapefruit size
cosmicInflation.evidence: CMB uniformity, quantum fluctuations became seeds for galaxies
cosmicInflation.multiverse: Eternal inflation theory suggests infinite universes

cosmicMicrowaveBackground.description: Afterglow of Big Bang, oldest light in universe
cosmicMicrowaveBackground.significance: Smoking gun evidence for Big Bang
cosmicMicrowaveBackground.information: Reveals age, composition, and geometry of universe

visible Matter.description: Everything we can see - stars, galaxies, planets, us

darkMatter.description: Invisible matter detected only by gravity
evidence: Galaxy rotation curves don't match visible mass
Gravitational lensing shows more mass than visible
darkMatter.detection: Direct detection experiments ongoing, none confirmed

darkEnergy.description: Mysterious energy causing universe to expand faster
darkEnergy.effect: Acts like anti-gravity, pushing space apart

theories.quintessence: Dynamic energy field changing over time
theories.modifiedGravity: Gravity works differently on cosmic scales

largeScaleStructure.description: How matter is distributed across universe

structure.groups: Small clusters of ~50 galaxies (like Local Group)
structure.voids: Vast empty regions 100-400 million light-years across

examples.greatAttractor: Massive gravitational anomaly pulling local galaxies
examples.shapley Supercluster: One of largest structures, ~25 galaxy clusters

expansion.hubbles Law: Galaxies recede at speed proportional to distance
expansion.tension: Different measurements give different values (Hubble tension)

observableUniverse.why Larger: Universe 13.8 billion years old but expansion made it larger
observableUniverse.horizon: We can only see to cosmic horizon (CMB)
observableUniverse.beyond: Universe continues beyond what we can see

bigFreeze.likely: Most likely scenario based on observations
bigFreeze.description: Universe expands forever, grows cold and dark

bigRip.description: Expansion accelerates until everything tears apart

bigCrunch.unlikely: If universe closed and dark energy reverses
bigCrunch.end: All matter crushed in reverse Big Bang

bigBounce.cyclic: Universe cycles through Big Bangs and Crunches

fateOfUniverse.current Consensus: Big Freeze most likely based on observations

levelI.name: Beyond Horizon
levelI.infinite: If universe is infinite, all possibilities exist somewhere

levelIII.name: Many Worlds
levelIII.branching: Universe branches with each quantum event
levelIII.parallel: You exist in all quantum branches

levelIV.name: Mathematical Universes
levelIV.description: All mathematical structures exist as universes

flat.evidence: CMB observations show universe is flat (within 0.4%)

shape.current: Observations indicate flat or very nearly flat

anthropicPrinciple.weak: Universe must be compatible with life observing it
anthropicPrinciple.strong: Universe must have properties allowing life to develop

fine Tuning.cosmologicalConstant: If 10^120 times larger, no structures form
fine Tuning.strong Force: If 1% stronger, no hydrogen; 1% weaker, only hydrogen
fine Tuning.massRatio: Proton/electron mass ratio must be precise

explanations.multiverse: Many universes, we're in one that allows life

horizonProblem.problem: Why is CMB so uniform if regions couldn't have communicated?
horizonProblem.solution: Inflation - everything was once in contact

flatnessProblem.problem: Why is universe so close to perfect flatness?
flatnessProblem.solution: Inflation - inflated any curvature to near-flatness

monopoleProblem.problem: Why don't we see magnetic monopoles predicted by GUTs?
monopoleProblem.solution: Inflation diluted them to undetectable levels

baryon Asymmetry.problem: Why is there more matter than antimatter?
baryon Asymmetry.expectation: Big Bang should create equal amounts
baryon Asymmetry.critical: Without asymmetry, no structures, no life

openQuestions: Why is there more matter than antimatter?
